🚀 ARIANE 09 | Blida, Algeria — From Blida to Beyond

We are a team of ambitious innovators from Blida, Algeria, passionate about space exploration, artificial intelligence, and building technology that solves real-world problems.

Our team brings experience in AI, software engineering, computer vision, optimization, and product development. We combine technical skills with an entrepreneurial mindset, aiming to turn scientific data into practical, interactive solutions.
summary: AquaState is a world water and climate observatory that answers one question at four scales — planet, country, region and dam: are we covered until the next rain? It fuses live NASA POWER/MERRA-2 climate records, NASA EONET events, GloFAS river discharge and World Bank indicators into WCRI-2.0, a transparent 0–100 resilience index scored for 249 countries across six pillars: water availability and storage, drought and soil, groundwater, flood, wildfire and desertification. Every score opens into its inputs, formula, source, confidence and freshness, then drills from the world map to a first-level region and a single reservoir. The dam layer catalogues 82,394 structures and tracks 33 monitored reservoirs, with the full deep index for 10 pilot dams. By turning scattered Earth data into a screening read that takes under a minute, AquaState helps water agencies, cities and journalists see where water stress is becoming climate risk — and exactly how much the data can support.
details:
What it does. AquaState is a working web application, not a concept page. It answers one question at four scales — planet, country, first-level region and single dam: how much water is stored, what pressure is acting on it, and when the next refill arrives. The overview is an interactive world choropleth of WCRI-2.0 with a country ranking, a distribution, active NASA EONET events and a snapshot history. A country sheet exposes the index arithmetic. The Map Viewer renders first-level regions (wilayas, states, provinces) for 209 countries from geoBoundaries ADM1 and samples the same live sources for each region. Dam pages carry the deep DRI, the Φ buffer bridge and historical analogs; a separate water-runway view answers the reservoir question directly.

How it works. One refresh orchestrator fetches NASA POWER/MERRA-2 monthly and daily records, NASA EONET open events, Open-Meteo forecasts, GloFAS river discharge and World Bank indicators. Every response is cached with a timestamp and a TTL, and the source ledger shows live, cached, error or missing. Six pillars are computed per country — water availability and storage (0.22), drought and soil (0.20), groundwater (0.14), flood (0.14), wildfire (0.14), desertification (0.16) — then combined with explicit weights and compounding penalties. Coverage below 40% of the weight is reported as NO_DATA, never as a score. The dam index preserves signed HRI mathematics (SSI, CMI, SRRI, SAI, EESI and the Φ buffer) and is locked by regression fixtures.

Why it matters. Water agencies, cities and journalists currently assemble this picture by hand from half a dozen portals. AquaState compresses that into under a minute while keeping provenance attached, so a number can be questioned and traced instead of trusted. It is deliberately a screening aid, not an operational warning system, and says so in the interface.

Built with. Python 3.14, Django 6.1, SQLite, vanilla JavaScript and Leaflet, with Natural Earth and geoBoundaries geometry. NASA POWER, NASA EONET, Open-Meteo, GloFAS and the World Bank provide data; Wikidata supplies the dam corpus; the index math uses NumPy and Pydantic. The 30-second film was captured with Playwright and composed with Pillow, NumPy/SciPy and FFmpeg. No API keys, no paid services and no LLM in the scoring path.

What makes it creative. The creative choice is refusal: instead of another opaque "AI risk score", the app exposes the arithmetic, coverage and freshness behind every number, and turns the storage question into a "water runway" measured in days. It also merges two originally separate projects — a country-scale water app and a dam-scale deep index — into one hierarchy (WCRI → WRI → DRI) where a forecast never rewrites an observation.

What we considered. Data honesty and failure modes; keyless, low-bandwidth operation; licence-clean imagery; reproducibility (58 Django tests and 122 pytest tests, including signed index fixtures); and the line between screening and operational claims. Reservoir storage is modelled/blended, groundwater is a labelled proxy, flood is river discharge — each limitation is visible in the product.
